title: Adaptive Admin Intake: Policy-driven RBAC & SCIM triage workflows
creator: Yara Martinez
description:
Context: Enterprise customers continue to submit heterogeneous admin/access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML mappings, SCIM provisioning rules, org policy exceptions). Current manual triage in Support/SE/CS is slow and inconsistent across accounts, causing SLA misses and security risk.

Objective: Build an adaptive, policy-driven intake and routing flow that classifies admin & access requests automatically, assigns risk/priority, and routes to the correct owner (Platform Security, Identity, Dedicated Ops, Solutions Engineering) with required approvals surfaced. The flow should support RBAC role templates, SSO/SAML mapping requests, SCIM sync/attribute change requests, and org-level policy exceptions.

Success metrics (initial):
- Median time-to-first-triage <= 4 hours for high-risk requests
- % of requests auto-routed correctly >= 65% in first 90 days
- SLA compliance (P1/P0) >= 99% within targeted pilot customers
- Reduction in Support->Eng handoffs for clarifications by 40%

Non-goals:
- Not implementing full automated enforcement of RBAC changes (that will be follow-up with Dedicated Ops).
- Not replacing Identity team's current SSO provider integrations; this is intake/triage only.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Intake form: add a structured admin request form in Console + a webhook-based intake endpoint for partners/CS. Form fields are schema-driven and include: request type, target org/tenant, role templates affected, SCIM attributes, justification/risk, requested timeline, attachments (audit logs), and customer contact.
2) Scoring engine: simple rule-based risk/priority scorer (policy rules + heuristics) that outputs {risk: low/medium/high, priority: P3..P0, route: team}. Rules to include: org size, role sensitivity, whether request impacts billing or data egress, presence of attachments, account tier. Scorer config stored as JSON in Config Service so rules are editable by PM/Security.
3) Routing: integrate with linear/jira flow to create a triage ticket pre-populated with structured metadata and suggested owner. For high-risk requests, enforce approval gating: request must be acknowledged by Security or Platform Owner before changes are allowed.
4) Audit & tracing: every intake instance must create an immutable audit record (Console + backend) and attach to the generated ticket; include links to customer-provided evidence and retention policy.
5) Feedback loop: add 'was this routing correct?' in triage UI; use feedback to iteratively improve scoring rules.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (Spike, 2 weeks): design schema for intake form, define initial scoring rules, mock UI; workshop with Security, Identity, Support, SE. Confluence design doc: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/20301234/Adaptive+Admin+Intake (placeholder).
- Phase 1 (MVP, 4 weeks): Console form + backend intake endpoint + rule-based scorer + create pre-populated Linear ticket; pilot with 3 enterprise customers.
- Phase 2 (Hardening, 6 weeks): Approval gating, audit retention, telemetry dashboards in Console (triage time, auto-route accuracy), integration with Dedicated Ops runbook for role deployment.
- Phase 3 (Scale): Expand request types, integrate SCIM bulk change workflows, expose intake API for partner automation.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Rule-based scorer vs ML classifier: rule-based is auditable and faster to ship but may require manual tuning; ML could improve accuracy but needs labeled data and introduces explainability concerns. Recommend rule-based for MVP with ability to import ML later.
- Where to store templates and auditable config: Config Service vs Console DB. Config Service preferred for feature-flagging and rollouts.
- Approval UX: inline in Console vs email-based approvals. Inline provides immediate traceability; email supports external approvers. MVP = inline + email notifications.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Structured intake form in Console accessible to enterprise admin and CS web hook.
- Intake creates a Linear ticket with standardized labels, metadata, and audit link.
- Rule-based scorer returns a routing decision for >80% of test cases defined in PRD.
- Triage dashboard shows time-to-first-triage and auto-route rate.
- Basic feedback input available to triagers.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Yara Martinez (owner)
- Eng leads: Liam Chen (platform), Priya Kapoor (identity)
- Security: Jonah Patel
- Support/CS: Ana Gomez
- Design: Mei Huang

Dependencies: ENG-1842 (intake webhook infra), ENG-2076 (audit log pipeline), PM-9951 (enterprise admin intake contract references), legal/compliance review for retention.

Risks:
- Mis-classification could surface sensitive changes to wrong team. Mitigation: conservative default routing to Security for 'unknown' or high-risk.
- Customers might submit incomplete evidence; include clear required/optional fields and CS checklist.

Rollout plan: pilot with 3 customers (two large, one mid-market) for 6 weeks, measure metrics, iterate rules, then ramp to all enterprise accounts in 2026-Q2.
